title: Inulin: what it means for your plan
standfirst: Which of our plan rules this ingredient turns on, and what that does not tell you.

spans.text: Inulin is a soluble dietary fibre made of fructose chains, extracted mainly from chicory root, used as a fibre source and to add bulk or replace sugar and fat.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use inulin as a fibre/bulking agent and it is of plant origin.
Our scorer looks for inulin when Low-FODMAP is on for you. If that plan is off, your score does not change. This is how the app reads a label. It is not a claim about health.
Labels do not all use the same word for this. Below is every spelling we watch for. Some come from other languages, because a pack made for another country prints its own.
One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
